Plant|date=2016-12-11|website=interestingengineering.com|language=en-US|access-date=2020-03-13}} == History == The company was incorporated on 23 January 2016, as Adani Green Energy Limited under the [[Companies Act 2013]].{{Cite web|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/adani-green-energy-ltd/infocompanyhistory/companyid-64847.cms|title=Adani Green Energy History {{!}} Adani Green Energy Information |website=Economic Times|access-date=2020-03-05}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/company/adani-green-70666/information/company-history|title=Adani Green Energy Ltd.|work=Business Standard India|access-date=2020-03-05}} During the initial days of existence, AGEL and Inox Wind together established a 20 MW capacity wind power project in Lahori, [[Madhya Pradesh]].{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/energy/power/inox-wind-bags-two-70-mw-wind-energy-projects-from-adani-green/articleshow/51792352.cms?from=mdr|title=Inox Wind bags two 70-MW wind energy projects from Adani Green|date=2016-04-12|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2020-03-05}} Also, AGEL bought Inox Wind's 50 MW wind power project at Dayapar village in [[Kutch]]. The project was conceived by the latter when it won a [[Solar Energy Corporation of India]]'s capacity bids for wind power projects connected to the [[National Grid (India)|National Grid]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.bloombergquint.com/business/inox-wind-closes-deal-to-sell-50-mw-wind-project-to-adani-green-energy|title=Inox Wind Closes Deal To Sell 50 MW Wind Project To Adani Green Energy|website=BloombergQuint|date=16 October 2019 |language=en|access-date=2020-03-12}} In 2015–2016, Adani Renewable Energy Park Limited, a subsidiary of AGEL, signed a [[joint venture]] agreement with the [[Government of Rajasthan]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/national/adani-rajasthan-govt-form-jt-venture-to-set-up-solar-park/article7318806.ece|title=Adani, Rajasthan govt form jt venture to set up solar park|website=@businessline|date=15 June 2015 |language=en|access-date=2020-03-05}} In 2017, the company took the complete control of overall solar energy portfolio of [[Adani Enterprises]] and got itself listed at [[National Stock Exchange of India]] and [[Bombay Stock Exchange]].{{Cite web|url=https://mnacritique.mergersindia.com/adani-renewable-energy-demerger/|title=Adani Enterprises to demerge renewable energy business|last=Jain|first=Hiteshkumar|date=2017-12-11|website=M&A Critique|language=en-US|access-date=2020-03-12}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.saurenergy.com/solar-energy-news/adani-enterprises-to-demerge-renewable-energy-business-to-simplify-structure|title=Adani Enterprises to Demerge Renewable Energy Business to Simplify Structure|website=www.saurenergy.com|access-date=2020-03-12}} In 2022, Adani Green Energy Limited had a market cap of Rs. 3,26,635.42 crore.{{Cite web |title=Top 100 stocks by Market Capitalization {{!}} BSE Listed stocks Market Capitalization |url=https://www.bseindia.com/markets/equity/eqreports/topmarketcapitalization.aspx |access-date=2022-12-19 |website=www.bseindia.com}} == Operations == Currently, the company manages 5,290 MW of wind energy and solar power plants including 46 operational projects in 11 states of [[India]] namely [[Uttar Pradesh]], [[Rajasthan]], [[Punjab, India|Punjab]], [[Maharashtra]], [[Gujarat]], [[Madhya Pradesh]], [[Chhattisgarh]], [[Andhra Pradesh]], [[Karnataka]], [[Tamil Nadu]], and [[Telangana]]. AGEL has a current project portfolio of ~5.29 GW and an operational capacity of ~2.36 GW.{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/energy/power/adani-green-energy-arm-bags-130-mw-wind-power-project-from-seci/articleshow/69874616.cms?from=mdr|title=Adani Green Energy arm bags 130-MW wind power project from SECI|date=2019-06-20|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2020-03-05}} As of 31 March 2019, AGEL has one joint venture and 39 subsidiaries.{{Cite web|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/annual-report/adanigreenenergylimited/directors-report/ADANI54145|title=Adani Green Energy Limited Directors Report, Adani Green Ene Reports by Directors|website=www.moneycontrol.com|language=en|access-date=2020-03-05}} In May 2020, AGEL won the world's largest solar bid worth $6 billion by the [[Solar Energy Corporation of India]] (SECI). The bid entails AGEL building an 8000 MW photovoltaic power plant.{{Cite news|author=|date=2020-06-09|title=Adani Green hits new high on winning world's largest solar bid worth $6 bn|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/markets/adani-green-hits-new-high-stock-zooms-127-in-three-months-120060900281_1.html|access-date=2020-06-30}}{{Cite web|date=2020-06-09|title=Adani wins world's largest solar project; to invest Rs 45,000 crore|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/industry/adani-wins-worlds-largest-solar-project-to-invest-rs-45000-crore/1986420/|access-date=2020-06-10|website=The Financial Express|language=en-US}} In May 2021, AGEL confirmed its decision to buy [[SoftBank Group|SoftBank Group Corp]] backed SB Energy Holdings Limited for $3.5 billion.{{Cite web|agency=Reuters|author=Anuron Kumar Mitra|title=India's Adani Green to buy SoftBank-backed SB Energy in $3.5 billion deal|url=https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/indias-adani-green-to-buy-softbank-backed-sb-energy-in-%243.5-billion-deal-2021-05-18|access-date=2021-05-19|website=Nasdaq|language=en}} According to media reports, The Khavda renewable energy plant was initiated in December 2022, and its first production occurred on 31 December 2023.The plant covers an area of 538 square kilometers. The hybrid renewable energy cluster generates solar energy during the day and wind energy in the evening, with an operational capacity of 2,000 MW of solar energy.{{cite web | last=Walia | first=Aggam | title=With core assets in Khavda & Mundra, Kachchh becomes central to Adani’s green ambitions | website=The Indian Express | date=8 Apr 2024 | url=https://indianexpress.com/article/business/economy/with-core-assets-in-khavda-mundra-kachchh-becomes-central-to-adanis-green-ambitions-9257059/ | access-date=20 Aug 2024}}{{cite web | title=Adani Green's Khavda power plant world's largest, five times the size of Paris | website=The Economic Times | date=7 Apr 2024 | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/renewables/adani-greens-khavda-power-plant-worlds-largest-five-times-the-size-of-paris/articleshow/109107172.cms?utm_source=contentofinterest&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=cppst | access-date=20 Aug 2024}} The wind turbines used at Khavda had a capacity of 5.2 MW each, based on German designs and manufactured at Adani Group facilities near Mundra Port. According to the report, it supplied electricity to millions of households annually and reduced carbon dioxide emissions by an estimated 58 million tonnes per year.{{cite web | last=Mishra | first=Lalatendu | title=Adani Green Energy commissions 480 MW solar and wind energy capacity; on track to complete world’s largest RE park at Khavda | website=The Hindu | date=2025-04-01 | url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/adani-green-energy-commissions-480-mw-solar-and-wind-energy-capacity-on-track-to-complete-worlds-largest-re-park-at-khavda/article69397294.ece | access-date=2025-08-16}}{{cite web | title=Adani Green Energy operationalises 250 MW wind capacity at Khavda, Gujarat | website=ETEnergyworld.com | date=2024-07-24 | url=https://energy.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/renewable/adani-green-energy-operationalises-250-mw-wind-capacity-at-khavda-gujarat/111988510 | access-date=2025-08-16}} The site also featured waterless robotic cleaning systems for solar panels to reduce water consumption in the arid environment. In 2024, United States Ambassador Eric Garcetti visited the Khavda site and highlighted its role in the US–India partnership on clean energy.{{cite web | title=US Ambassador Eric Garcetti hails Adani's Khavda renewable energy project | website=The Economic Times | date=2024-07-18 | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/renewables/us-ambassador-eric-garcetti-hails-adanis-khavda-renewable-energy-project/articleshow/111833102.cms?from=mdr | access-date=2025-08-16}} == Green bonds == In late 2019, AGEL became the first Indian company to offer investment-grade US dollar [[green bond]]s worth US$362.5 million{{Cite web|url=https://www.saurenergy.com/solar-energy-news/adani-green-energys-362-5-mn-green-bonds-attracts-strong-interest|title=Adani Green Energy's $362.5 mn Green Bonds Attracts Strong Interest|website=www.saurenergy.com|access-date=2020-03-12}} to foreign investors.{{Cite web|url=https://esg.theasset.com/ESG/39820/the-asset-talk-adani-green-energy-us3625-million-amortizing-senior-secured-green-bond|title=The Asset Talk: Adani Green Energy US$362.5 million amortizing senior secured green bond|website=esg.theasset.com|language=en|access-date=2020-03-12}} The bonds got listed on Singapore Exchange Securities Trading Limited (SGX- ST) on 15 October 2019{{Cite web|url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/markets/adani-green-energy-arms-to-issue-bonds-worth-362-5-million-4504341.html|title=Adani Green Energy arms to issue bonds worth $362.5 million|website=Moneycontrol|date=4 October 2019 |access-date=2020-03-12}} and it will mature on the same date in 2039.{{Cite USD 362.50 million Green Bonds|date=2019-10-04|work=Business Standard India|access-date=2020-03-12}} == Acquisitions == In March 2018, upon acquisition of 49 percent equity shares of Kodangal Solar Parks Private Limited, the latter became a joint venture of AGEL. In 2019, AGEL acquired the rest 51 percent equity share as well.{{Cite web|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/adani-green-energy-acquires-remaining-51-per-cent-stake-in-kodangal-solar-parks/article25980090.ece|title=Adani Green Energy acquires remaining 51 per cent stake in Kodangal Solar Parks|last=PTI|website=@businessline|date=12 January 2019 |language=en|access-date=2020-03-12}}{{Cite news|agency=Press Trust of India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/adani-green-energy-acquires-remaining-51-stake-in-kodangal-solar-parks-119011200552_1.html|title=Adani Green Energy acquires remaining 51% stake in Kodangal Solar Parks|date=2019-01-12|work=Business Standard India|access-date=2020-03-12}} In mid-2019, AGEL acquired [[Essel Group]]'s solar power portfolio of 205 MW located in [[Punjab, India|Punjab]], [[Karnataka]] and [[Uttar Pradesh]] for US$185 million (approx. ₹1,300 crores).{{Cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/industry/energy/essel-group-in-talks-with-adani-to-sell-solar-energy-assets-1569517438223.html|title=Essel Group in talks with Adani to sell solar energy assets|last=Thomas|first=Tanya|date=2019-09-26|website=Livemint|language=en|access-date=2020-03-12}} AGEL has also agreed to buy out the remaining 480 MW solar energy portfolio of the former which are under construction.{{Cite news|last=Laghate|first=Gaurav|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/energy/power/adani-green-may-buy-rest-of-essels-480-mw-solar-assets/articleshow/72701862.cms?from=mdr|title=Adani Green may buy rest of Essel's 480-MW solar assets|date=2019-12-15|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2020-03-12}} In early 2020, French energy company TotalEnergies entered into a binding agreement with AGEL for the investment of US$510 million to acquire a 20% stake in the latter.{{Cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/small-biz/productline/power-generation/adani-green-energy-surges-after-signing-deal-with-total-for-510-million/articleshow/74133215.cms|title=Adani Green Energy surges after signing deal with Total for $510 million|date=2020-02-14|work=The Economic Times|access-date=2020-03-12}}{{Cite news|last=Market|first=Capital|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/news-cm/adani-green-energy-signs-deal-for-total-s-investment-of-usd-510-mn-in-solar-venture-120021400317_1.html|title=Adani Green Energy signs deal for Total's investment of USD 510 mn in solar venture|date=2020-02-14|work=Business Standard India|access-date=2020-03-12}}{{Cite web |date=2021-01-18 |title=Total to Acquire 20% of AGEL the Largest Solar Developer in the World |url=https://totalenergies.com/media/news/press-releases/total-to-acquire-20-percent-of-AGEL-the-largest-solar-developer-in-the-world |access-date=2024-04-27 |website=TotalEnergies.com |language=en}} In May 2021, AGEL acquired [[SoftBank Group|SoftBank Group Corp]] backed SB Energy Holdings Limited for $3.5 billion. == Controversies == === Rajasthan Solar Park === Local farmers have opposed to construction of 1.5 GW solar park at [[Pokhran]] after which High Court of Rajasthan has ordered status quo.{{Cite news|agency=Press Trust India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/raj-hc-temporarily-stays-adani-s-1500-mw-solar-power-project-near-pokhran-120090802001_1.html|access-date=2021-03-10}} ===Allegations of extract: Adani Green Energy Limited (AGEL) is an Indian renewable energy company, headquartered in Ahmedabad, India. It is majority-owned by the Indian conglomerate Adani Group, which is a major international coal-mining enterprise, and minority-owned by TotalEnergies. The company operates Kamuthi Solar Power Project, one of the largest solar photovoltaic plants in the world.
